_comment: Virgil's glossary — plain-language entries for UI names and readouts. Hand-written; config, committed. Keys are lowercase snake_case and must never equal a module key (module descriptions come from their docstrings, through Daedalus). Each text: one or two sentences, ending in a period, at most 240 characters.

home.label: Felhaven
home.text: Home. Talk to Pythia here; her language model runs on this PC, not in the cloud.

chronometry.label: Chronometry
chronometry.text: Time awareness: the date, the time, the season, and where the day stands.

moderati.label: Moderati
moderati.text: The machine looking at itself: vitals, network, logs, keys, settings, and a map of its own modules.

atmospherics.label: Atmospherics
atmospherics.text: Weather for your location, now and in the days ahead, with sunrise, sunset and the moon.

navigation.label: Navigation
navigation.text: Charts and maps. Open it to find the Celestarium and the Cartograph.

celestarium.label: Celestarium
celestarium.text: A map of the sky overhead right now, with constellation stories and tonight's viewing conditions.

cartograph.label: Cartograph
cartograph.text: A local map: terrain, water and roads around one point, saved so it still works offline.

dynastic_vault.label: Dynastic Vault
dynastic_vault.text: Finance, behind Cerberus's lock: prices for a watchlist, and a buy and sell ledger you keep by hand.

scriptorium.label: Scriptorium
scriptorium.text: News. Headlines from the feeds you chose, each one linking back to where it came from.

vox_array.label: Vox Array
vox_array.text: Audio: music from YouTube, text turned into audio files, playback of those files, and the Auto-DJ's memory.

cogitator.label: Cogitator
cogitator.text: Small utilities: a to-do list and notes, a calculator, and a unit converter.

cpu.label: CPU
cpu.text: The processor, the part that does the computing. Spikes are normal; pinned near 100% for minutes means something is working it hard.

ram.label: RAM
ram.text: Short-term working memory, where programs keep what they're using right now. Busy is fine; near 100% for a long stretch makes everything slow.

disk.label: Disk
disk.text: Long-term storage, where files stay when the PC is off. This shows how full the drive is; leave some room free for Windows and updates.

wifi.label: Wi-Fi
wifi.text: Whether this PC's Wi-Fi adapter is connected. Connected isn't the same as online; the next row says that.

internet.label: Internet
internet.text: Whether the internet actually answers. "limited" usually means a sign-in page is in the way, like hotel or campground Wi-Fi.

ollama.label: Ollama
ollama.text: The program that runs Pythia's language model on this PC. If it's offline, Pythia can't answer.

boot_drive.label: Boot drive
boot_drive.text: The drive Windows starts from, where updates and caches pile up. It is usually the one that fills first, so leave it some room.

uptime.label: Uptime
uptime.text: How long since this PC last restarted. Some Windows updates only finish on a restart.

gpu.label: GPU
gpu.text: The graphics card. Besides drawing the screen, it runs Pythia's language model, far faster than the processor could.

gpu_memory.label: GPU memory
gpu_memory.text: Memory on the graphics card. Pythia's model has to fit here to answer quickly; what doesn't fit spills to the slower processor.

gpu_load.label: GPU load
gpu_load.text: How hard the graphics card is working right now. It jumps while Pythia writes an answer.

loaded_model.label: Loaded model
loaded_model.text: The language model Ollama is holding in memory, and how much of it fits on the graphics card. All of it on the GPU is the fast case.

weather_alert.label: Weather alerts
weather_alert.text: The National Weather Service's warnings, watches and advisories for your coordinates, checked once a minute. A warning means act now; a watch means be ready; an advisory means take care.

alert_severity.label: Severity
alert_severity.text: How much harm the Weather Service expects: Minor, Moderate, Severe or Extreme.

alert_certainty.label: Certainty
alert_certainty.text: How sure the Weather Service is that it will happen: Observed, Likely, Possible or Unlikely.

space_weather.label: Space weather
space_weather.text: NOAA's three storm scales, 0 (none) to 5 (extreme). R: radio blackouts from solar flares. S: solar radiation storms. G: geomagnetic storms, which bring the aurora; Kp is their 0 to 9 index.

aurora_estimate.label: Aurora here
aurora_estimate.text: A rough guide from NOAA's rule of thumb: the aurora reaches about 2 degrees of magnetic latitude further per Kp step. It needs a dark, clear sky too.

atmos_place.label: Place
atmos_place.text: Whose weather NOW and FORECAST show: Home, or an area saved in the Cartograph. Warnings, sun, moon and space weather stay on Home.

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.text: The air temperature now. It turns amber when hot or cold (80°F/27°C and up, 40°F/4°C and below) and red when dangerous (95°F/35°C, 20°F/−7°C).

feels_like.label: Feels like
feels_like.text: How the air feels on skin: wind makes cold feel colder, and humidity makes heat feel hotter.

high_low.label: High / low
high_low.text: Today's forecast high and low temperatures.

wind.label: Wind
wind.text: Wind speed in miles per hour, and in words: calm under 5, a light breeze under 15, moderate under 25, strong under 40, very strong beyond.

humidity.label: Humidity
humidity.text: Relative humidity: how close the air is to holding all the water vapour it can. High humidity makes heat feel worse and fog more likely.

rain_chance.label: Rain chance
rain_chance.text: Today's highest chance of rain in any part of the day, not the chance that it rains all day.

uv_index.label: UV index
uv_index.text: How strong the sun's burning rays are right now: 0–2 low, 3–5 moderate, 6–7 high, 8–10 very high, 11 and up extreme.

forecast_day.label: Forecast day
forecast_day.text: The day's sky, its high and low, and its highest chance of rain or snow, whichever is larger. A dash means neither.

sun_times.label: Sunrise and sunset
sun_times.text: When the top edge of the sun crosses the horizon here, worked out on this PC from your coordinates and the date.

golden_hour.label: Golden hour
golden_hour.text: Around sunrise and around sunset, when low sunlight is warm and soft. Felhaven counts the sun's angle: from 4° below the horizon to 6° above it.

day_length.label: Day length
day_length.text: Time from sunrise to sunset. Around the equinoxes it changes by a few minutes a day; around the solstices, hardly at all.

moon_phase.label: Moon phase
moon_phase.text: How much of the moon is lit, and whether that is growing (waxing) or shrinking (waning). One full cycle takes about 29.5 days.

moon_illumination.label: Illumination
moon_illumination.text: How much of the moon's face is lit as seen from Earth: 0% at new moon, 100% at full.

moon_times.label: Moonrise and moonset
moon_times.text: When the top edge of the moon crosses the horizon here. It comes about 50 minutes later each day, so on some days it doesn't rise or set at all: a dash.

radio_blackouts.label: Radio blackouts
radio_blackouts.text: Solar flares' X-rays disrupting shortwave radio on Earth's sunlit side, from R1 (minor) to R5 (extreme). They last minutes to hours.

solar_radiation_storms.label: Solar radiation storms
solar_radiation_storms.text: Fast protons from the sun, from S1 to S5. They matter to satellites, astronauts and polar flights, not to people on the ground.

geomagnetic_storms.label: Geomagnetic storms
geomagnetic_storms.text: Disturbances of Earth's magnetic field after a solar outburst, from G1 to G5 (Kp 5 to 9). They bring the aurora toward the equator and can trouble power grids and GPS.

space_outlook.label: Next 3 days
space_outlook.text: NOAA's forecast: the geomagnetic storm level expected each day, and the highest chance of a solar flare strong enough for a radio blackout (R1 or more).

vox_response.label: Vox Response
vox_response.text: When lit, Pythia reads each answer aloud as she writes it. Click to turn it on or off.

vox_end.label: Vox End
vox_end.text: Stops the answer being written and anything being spoken. It is lit while there is something to stop, and it works either way.

auto_dj.label: Auto-DJ
auto_dj.text: When lit, each time a song ends the next one is chosen from what you have played before, and introduced aloud. It turns itself off after three turns that play nothing.

reset_session.label: Reset Session
reset_session.text: Clears the conversation, Pythia's memory of it and the session counters, and stops anything being written or spoken.

cerberus_lamp.label: Cerberus
cerberus_lamp.text: The lock on the key vault. Dim is sealed, amber is open, and red means a tamper alarm: see the Cerberus tab in Moderati.

scraptoken_flux.label: Scraptoken Flux
scraptoken_flux.text: Tokens used this session, counting what Pythia read and what she wrote. A token is roughly three quarters of a word.

rites.label: Rites
rites.text: Tool calls Pythia has made this session, such as a weather or clock lookup. A red count beside it is how many failed.

ammit_badge.label: Ammit
ammit_badge.text: The countdown timer from Chronometry. Dim is idle, amber is running, red is time's up, and green is an alarm you have dismissed.

status_line.label: Status
status_line.text: What Pythia or the Auto-DJ is doing right now. When it shows how many songs are queued, click it to see them.

foe_version.label: Version
foe_version.text: The version of FOE that is running: the newest audit mark in Felhaven's own code, read when it started. It changes when an audit lands, never by hand.

speak_aloud.label: Speak aloud
speak_aloud.text: Reads this one answer aloud, in place of anything being spoken.

answer_stats.label: Answer stats
answer_stats.text: Tokens, time taken, tokens per second and tool calls for this answer. Click a tool count to open the Rite Log, the record of each call.

file_change.label: File change
file_change.text: Pythia may change a file only after ALLOW. DENY, Vox End, Reset Session, closing the window or waiting too long all mean no.

transport_prev.label: Previous
transport_prev.text: Goes back to the previous track in the playlist. Dim while the player isn't running: play something first.

transport_play.label: Play or pause
transport_play.text: Pauses the track, or carries on from where it stopped. Dim while the player isn't running: play something first.

transport_next.label: Next
transport_next.text: Skips to the next track in the playlist. Dim while the player isn't running: play something first.

transport_stop.label: Stop
transport_stop.text: Stops what is playing. Dim while there is nothing to stop.

playlist_save.label: Save playlist
playlist_save.text: Adds the label and the address typed here to your saved playlists.

playlist_remove.label: Remove playlist
playlist_remove.text: Takes this playlist off your saved list. Click once and it asks "remove?"; click again within a few seconds to confirm.

search_save.label: Save result
search_save.text: Saves this result to your playlists. A tick means it is saved.

file_remove.label: Remove file
file_remove.text: Sends this audio file to the Recycle Bin. Click once and it asks "remove?"; click again within a few seconds to confirm.

task_check.label: Done
task_check.text: Marks the task done, or not done again.

task_delete.label: Delete task
task_delete.text: Deletes this task at once. There is no undo.

ammit_minutes.label: Minutes
ammit_minutes.text: Type a number of minutes, then press Enter or the play button to start the countdown.

ammit_run.label: Start or pause
ammit_run.text: Starts the countdown, pauses it, or carries on from where it paused.

ammit_reset.label: Reset
ammit_reset.text: Clears the countdown back to zero.

open_story.label: Open story
open_story.text: Teal means the headline opens in your browser when you click it. Grey means the feed gave no link.

map_zoom.label: Zoom
map_zoom.text: How far the chart is magnified; the mouse wheel over the chart changes it too. At 2× and 4× you can drag the chart to look around.

map_home.label: Home
map_home.text: Brings the chart back to your own location and clears the search.

scrapstream.label: Scrapstream
scrapstream.text: Every feed's headlines in one list, newest first. Each feed is capped so a busy one can't crowd out the rest.

source_fonts.label: Source Fonts
source_fonts.text: The same headlines sorted by where they came from, one fold for each feed. Click a feed's name to open or close it.

playlists_tab.label: Playlists
playlists_tab.text: Your saved playlists. Click one to play it, or add another with the label and address boxes.

search_tab.label: Search
search_tab.text: Searches YouTube by name. Click a result to play it, or its plus sign to save it.

net_connections.label: Connections
net_connections.text: Programs on this PC that are talking to another computer right now, and the address at the other end. EST means connected; the other codes are a connection opening or closing.

net_listening.label: Listening
net_listening.text: Programs waiting for something to connect to them, and the address and port each one waits on.

net_traffic.label: Traffic
net_traffic.text: How fast data is leaving (▲) and arriving (▼), in total and for each network adapter.

net_dns.label: DNS cache
net_dns.text: Site names this PC looked up recently, and the addresses they led to.

net_firewall.label: Firewall
net_firewall.text: Whether Windows Firewall is on for each kind of network: domain, private and public.

net_timeline.label: Timeline
net_timeline.text: Connections that opened (＋) or closed (－) while Felhaven has been watching.

vault_keys.label: Vault
vault_keys.text: The API keys Felhaven uses, encrypted to this Windows account. A key stays masked until you click reveal.

vault_custody.label: Custody
vault_custody.text: The settings files Cerberus watches over. Click one to open it in your editor.

vault_ledger.label: Ledger
vault_ledger.text: A record of each unlock, lock and key access, newest first.

sky_preset.label: Sky presets
sky_preset.text: Shows the sky from somewhere else: the North Pole, the equator or the South Pole. Current brings back your own sky. Local conditions hide while a preset is on.

sky_clarity.label: Clarity
sky_clarity.text: How clear the sky is for stargazing, from cloud cover: five stars is a clear sky, none is overcast.

map_cache_status.label: Map cache
map_cache_status.text: Whether the map data for this area is saved on this PC, so the chart works offline. NOT CACHED means press CACHE AREA first.

cache_area.label: Cache area
cache_area.text: Downloads the terrain, water and roads around this spot and saves them. Click once to see the size, again to start.

cached_areas.label: Cached areas
cached_areas.text: Every map area saved on this PC, nearest your location first. Click this header to open or fold the list; click a name to view that area.

area_rename.label: Rename area
area_rename.text: Gives this area a name of your own. Type it and press Enter; Escape or clicking away keeps the old name.

area_refresh.label: Refresh area
area_refresh.text: Downloads this area's terrain, water and roads again, often tens of megabytes. Click once and it asks "refresh?"; click again within a few seconds to start.

area_delete.label: Delete area
area_delete.text: Moves this area's saved map to the Recycle Bin. Click once and it asks "delete?"; click again within a few seconds to confirm.

ledger_action.label: Buy or sell
ledger_action.text: Picks whether the row you are adding is a buy or a sell. Click to switch; + ADD records it.

base_copy.label: Base copy
base_copy.text: A saved copy of the song list to go back to if an edit goes wrong. Its date and size are beside it.

base_restore.label: Restore
base_restore.text: Loads the base copy into the box above. Nothing changes until you press SAVE.

base_take.label: Take from saved
base_take.text: Makes the song list as it is saved now the new base copy. Save your edits first.

calc_ans.label: ANS
calc_ans.text: The last answer. Type ans in an expression to use it again.

log_status.label: Log status
log_status.text: Green: only routine lines. Amber: a warning in the last few minutes. Red: something failed. The list below has the details.

network_summary.label: Network summary
network_summary.text: How many connections are live, how many ports programs listen on, the traffic and whether the firewall is on. Teal means Argus can read everything Windows lets it; amber means part of the picture is missing. It never judges a connection.

import_legend.label: Legend
import_legend.text: The colours show the kind of module: core, tool or panel. A solid line is an import loaded at start-up; a dotted one is loaded only when needed.

llm_model.label: Model
llm_model.text: The language model Pythia thinks with, from the ones Ollama has installed that can use tools. A new pick unloads the old one, so the next answer is slow.

llm_thinking.label: Thinking
llm_thinking.text: When on, Pythia reasons before she answers. Answers are slower and more careful, and the reasoning is never shown.

llm_temperature.label: Temperature
llm_temperature.text: How much Pythia varies her wording. Lower is steadier and more predictable, higher is livelier. DEFAULT leaves it to the model.

queue_remove.label: Remove from queue
queue_remove.text: Click a song to take it off the queue at once. There is no confirm: Auto-DJ tops the queue back up within a few songs anyway.

rite_status.label: Status
rite_status.text: ✓ ok: the tool answered. ⚠ failed: it returned an error, explained below. ○ not run: the turn was stopped before this call ran. The time is how long it took.

rite_select.label: Select
rite_select.text: Click a rite's name to select it for COPY THIS RITE; click it again to clear.

rite_expand.label: Show or hide
rite_expand.text: Click to open or close this field. The result preview starts closed because it can be long; truncated means it was cut for this window.

rite_copy.label: Copy this rite
rite_copy.text: Copies the selected rite's record as JSON, ready to paste into a bug report. Dim until you click a rite's name.
